previous.passage: We ran a tailoring shop on a street in Tehran that had too many tailors, and by the third winter the ledger was mostly red. My brother Kemoy cut the cloth; I, Hemi, did the seams, the buttonholes, the slow finishing. When a colonel's wife praised a coat in the window, Kemoy accepted her compliments at the counter while I sat in the back with pins in my mouth. I said nothing then, and I said a good deal later, on the roof, where we hung the shop's linen to dry. For a month after that we pinned our cloths at opposite ends of the line. In March the colonel's wife returned for a second coat and asked for the tailor who had finished the first. Kemoy did not answer her. He walked to the back of the shop, took my hand, which was still holding a needle, and led me out to the counter. That evening on the roof he hung his cloths next to mine.
previous.question: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
options: A failing shop strains two brothers who share the work of making each coat.
A customer's return allows the narrator to receive praise for his careful finishing.
The brothers' quarrel on the roof is what drives the colonel's wife to return.
An earlier slight over recognition is repaired through an act instead of an apology.
previous.explanation: 첫 사건에서 형 Kemoy는 손님의 칭찬을 혼자 받고, 마무리 작업을 한 화자는 뒤편에 앉아 있다가 나중에 옥상에서 따진다. 중간에는 한 달 동안 빨랫줄 양 끝에 따로 빨래를 너는 미해결 장면이 놓인다. 뒷사건에서 Kemoy는 아무 말 없이 화자의 손을 잡고 계산대로 데려가므로, 공로를 둘러싼 서운함이 사과의 말 대신 행동으로 회복되었다는 D가 정답이다. A는 첫 사건만, B는 둘째 사건만 요약했고, C는 다툼과 손님 재방문 사이의 인과를 지문에 없게 세운 선택지다.

previous.passage: Dry leaves filled the stone basin of the fountain in our courtyard in Taipei, and every autumn Baoyu came to argue with me about them. He was my father's oldest friend, and he arrived each October with a rake, insisting that the leaves be burned, while I insisted they be left for mulch. My father had sailed for Fujian when I was nine and had sent two letters since. Baoyu never spoke of him. We argued about leaves for six autumns, loudly enough that the neighbors leaned out of their windows. One year he brought a small tin box along with the rake and set it on the fountain's rim; I did not open it, and he did not mention it. The seventh October he did not come. A boy brought the rake and the tin box to the gate with a note in Baoyu's hand: the leaves are yours to decide now. Inside the box were my father's letters to him, thirty of them, every one asking about me.
previous.question: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
options: A minor yearly dispute proves to have stood in for a larger matter left unsaid.
An old family friend keeps up a garden custom after the narrator's father departs.
A box of letters shows that the narrator's father wrote more often than she knew.
The narrator's refusal to burn the leaves is what leads Baoyu to stop visiting.
